newsitem.title: UK: Asian demand, contango aid ailing W.Africa crudes.
newsitem.headline: Asian demand, contango aid ailing W.Africa crudes.

text.p: Strong Asian refinery demand for West African crude loading in early April and a contango -- pricing prompt barrels cheaper than forward oil -- are helping bolster sickly spot differentials, traders said on Tuesday.
At least 12 million barrels from Nigeria, Angola, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea are due to load in the first 10 days of April for refineries in South Korea, China and India.
Another two million barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe are due to sail for India later in the month, while Taiwan's CPC was looking on Tuesday for a VLCC for a first decade April trip.
Traders said sales of West African crude to Asia in April should rebound from March's depressed levels, despite a heavy programme of refinery maintenance in May.
"There's about 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) going already in April and we've seen relatively little done beyond the first decade so we think more will go," said a trader for an oil major.

Total exports in March averaged less than 500,000 bpd, down from over one million bpd in February, amid stiff competition from ample supply of regional crudes and strong Dated Brent quotes against which the Atlantic Basin crudes are priced.

With traders estimating scheduled maintenance programmes would shut in 1.5-2.0 million bpd of Asian refining capacity in May, they were wary of predicting a return to February's levels, the highest for 12 months.

But a wide open Brent/Dubai arbitrage, a 10 percent fall in Indonesian crude allocations in April, weak West African differentials and a contangoed physical Brent market were keeping Asian buyers interested, they said.
"You've got contango and you've got a refinery restart in Indonesia right now which means Minas (crude) supply is decreasing," said a trader.
Minas export allocations in April should average 61,000 bpd in April, down from 94,300 bpd in March, traders said on Monday.
On Saturday, Indonesian state oil company Pertamina restarted the crude distillation unit (CDU) at its 125,000 bpd Balongan refinery in West Java, shut on and off since February.
Dated Brent traded at May Brent -70 cents a barrel on Tuesday for a March 28-30 loader. Next week's Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) were priced at May Brent less 39 cents early on Tuesday.
Traders said South Korea's Yukong had taken advantage of the contango in physical crude markets to pick up a Qua Iboe/Zafiro combination for storage.
Bonny Light was pegged steady at Dated Brent +15/+20 cents on Tuesday, compared to its March OSP of Dated Brent +58 cents.
Spot Nigerian values buckled in early March, sliding to substantial discounts to the OSPs, and forcing one or two lifters to back out of end month commitments.
Traders said spot market activity was subdued on Tuesday, partly due to the absence of U.S. counterparties due to the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA) annual event.
